chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said: Abu Al-Khattab narrated to me in the best of conditions
He said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic
And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink

He said: And when Allah is mentioned alone, it is by the obedience of the one whom Allah commanded obedience to from the Progeny of Muhammad, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; and when those are mentioned whom Allah did not command obedience to, behold, they are joyful.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'when Allah alone is mentioned' refer to in Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: This hadith offers a distinctive Shia interpretation of Quran 39:45, linking the phrase 'Allah is mentioned alone' specifically to the obedience of the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby elevating their Wilayah to the status of divine remembrance. It contrasts the spiritual aversion of disbelievers to the mention of the Imams with their joy at the mention of other figures, underscoring the centrality of the Prophet's progeny in Islamic theology. This narration reinforces the concept that true monotheism (Tawhid) is inextricably linked to the acceptance of the Imams' authority.

en.hubeali: H 14919 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara who said, ‘Narrated to me Abu Al-Khattab in the best of conditions that:
He asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Statement of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic:
“[39:45] And when Allah alone is mentioned,

(the Imamasws said it is) by the obedience to the oneasws, the obedience to whomasws Allahazwj the One has Commanded for from the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww the hearts of those who do not believe in the hereafter shrink, and when there is a mention of the one, the obedience to whom Allahazwj has not Commanded for lo! they are joyful”.
en.sarwar: 472. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim the owner of the Barley, from Kaseer Bin Kalsama, who has narrated the following:
Imam (a.s.), said, regarding the Statement of Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic:
“[2:37] Then Adam received (some) words from his Lord”,

he (a.s.) said: ‘There is no god except You (azwj), Glory be to You (azwj) our Allah (azwj) and by Your (azwj) Praise, I have acted in an evil manner and have been unjust to myself, so Forgive me and You (azwj) are the best of the Forgivers. There is no god except You (azwj). Glory be to You (azwj) our Allah (azwj), and by Your (azwj) Praise. I have acted in an evil manner and have been unjust to myself, so Forgive me and be Merciful to me, and You (azwj) are the Most Merciful of the merciful ones. There is no god except You (azwj). Glory be to You (azwj) our Allah (azwj), and by Your (azwj) Praise. I have acted in an evil manner and have been unjust to myself, so Turn (with Forgiveness) to me for You (azwj) are the Merciful Forgiver’. And in another report regarding the Statement of the Mighty and Majestic: “[2:37] Then Adam received (some) words from his Lord”, he (a.s.) said: ‘He (as) asked for (forgiveness for) the sake of Muhammad (saww), and Ali (a.s.), and Al-Hassan (a.s.), and Al-Husayn (a.s.), and Fatima (a.s.)’.
